status: AUDITED AND LARGELY EXECUTED 2026-08-19 in adapted form (see audit_2026_08_19). Results live in the validation report and in C:/Users/abdallah/Desktop/ahmed/ezshop-saas/bench-iter2.
harness_notes: Each eval needs counterfactual configurations, not a with/without-skill pair. A configuration is a (model, effort, skills, context) tuple, so these must be run through named agent definitions or a Workflow script — the Agent tool alone cannot set effort or grant skills per call.

Recommended runner: define one agent definition per configuration under .claude/agents/, then execute each eval prompt once per configuration against a fresh copy of the fixture, saving ROUTE.md / ANSWER.md / transcript.md / metrics.json exactly as the iter1 and iter2 runs did.

Capture per run: model, effort, skills granted, total_tokens, duration_ms, total_tool_calls, subagent count. Report any metric the environment does not expose as unavailable rather than estimating it.
Risk-weight the grading. Missing a formatting inconsistency and missing a tenant leak are not the same defect, and an aggregate pass rate that treats them equally will recommend the wrong default.

skill_routing_evals.name: relevant-skill-inheritance
skill_routing_evals.question: Does a worker that clearly benefits from a specific installed skill actually receive it and follow it?
skill_routing_evals.prompt: Add a Filament resource for Products with a status filter and a bulk archive action, following how the rest of our admin panel is built.
expectations: The worker granted the framework skill uses the API surface that skill prescribes rather than a deprecated or invented one
The route names which skill was granted and why it was needed for this worker specifically
No skill unrelated to the admin-panel task is granted

skill_routing_evals.name: no-unnecessary-skills
skill_routing_evals.question: With many skills installed, does a tiny task stay at zero or one skill?
skill_routing_evals.prompt: Rename the ProductFilterData DTO to ProductQueryFilters and update its imports.
expectations: The router grants zero additional skills for this task
No delegation occurs at all
Total tool calls stay proportionate to a three-file rename (16 or fewer)
Granting the 8 unrelated skills measurably increases tokens or tool calls without improving the diff — record the delta as the cost of skill explosion

skill_routing_evals.name: parent-workflow-not-inherited
skill_routing_evals.question: When the coordinator is running a planning or orchestration workflow, is a mechanical child spared it?
skill_routing_evals.prompt: Coordinator is mid-way through a planning workflow. It needs one fact: which files reference ProductStatus.
configurations: haiku/low + the full parent workflow skill set
expectations: The child worker receives no planning or orchestration skill
The child receives a precise one-sentence assignment instead of the parent's workflow
The child's answer is at least as complete as the burdened configuration's, at lower token cost

skill_routing_evals.name: project-local-precedence
skill_routing_evals.question: Do project-local rules beat generic global guidance when they conflict?
skill_routing_evals.fixture_setup: Add a project skill at .claude/skills/project-conventions/SKILL.md stating that business logic lives in Actions and that a service layer is explicitly forbidden. Keep a generic global skill that recommends a service layer.
expectations: The implementation puts logic in an Action, following the project rule
The response states that the project convention governs where the two disagree
The generic recommendation is not applied silently over the project constraint

skill_routing_evals.name: skill-conflict-avoided
skill_routing_evals.question: Does the router avoid granting two skills that prescribe competing workflows?
skill_routing_evals.fixture_setup: Install two plausible testing-workflow skills with partly conflicting prescriptions (for example one mandating TDD-first, the other mandating implementation-then-characterisation tests).
skill_routing_evals.prompt: Add test coverage for the inventory reservation path.
expectations: Only one of the two testing workflows is granted
The choice is justified in one line by fit to the task
The worker does not attempt to satisfy both workflows simultaneously

skill_routing_evals.name: skill-improves-result
skill_routing_evals.question: Does the granted skill actually improve the outcome, or only the paperwork?
skill_routing_evals.prompt: Add an Orders index endpoint with filtering, sorting and permissions, consistent with the rest of the codebase.
expectations: Adherence to project conventions is higher with the skill (query builder usage, permission naming, resource shape, test layout)
The difference is in the delivered code, not merely in the explanation
If the outcomes are equivalent, record that the skill did not earn its context on this task

skill_routing_evals.name: context-overhead-of-skills
skill_routing_evals.question: What does an irrelevant skill bundle cost?
skill_routing_evals.prompt: Add a database index on orders.created_at.
expectations: Record tokens, tool calls and latency for both
Record any instance of the worker following guidance from an unrelated skill, or hedging between conflicting instructions
Use the measured delta to justify or refute the minimal-skill default — do not assume a direction

effort_routing_evals.name: normal-implementation
effort_routing_evals.prompt: Implement filtering and sorting for the products endpoint, consistent with the rest of the codebase.
effort_routing_evals.question: Does extra effort or capability buy enough on ordinary work to justify the cost? Expected answer: no — medium should be the default.

effort_routing_evals.name: difficult-debugging
effort_routing_evals.prompt: Checkout intermittently fails in production with insufficient stock errors, but works locally and stock levels look correct. Figure out what is going on.
effort_routing_evals.question: Does sonnet/high close the gap to opus/high on a genuinely hard diagnosis? This eval already has a known correct answer: the reservation leak (ReleaseStock has zero callers), not the read-compare-write race, which predicts the opposite symptom. Grade on which root cause each configuration lands on.

effort_routing_evals.name: architecture
effort_routing_evals.prompt: Define the inventory reservation contract and its transaction semantics so that overselling is impossible under concurrent checkout.
effort_routing_evals.question: What is the marginal value of each step? Report honestly if xhigh adds nothing over high.

effort_routing_evals.name: critical-review
effort_routing_evals.prompt: Review this diff for data-integrity and tenancy defects before it ships to production.
effort_routing_evals.fixture_setup: Use a diff seeded with known subtle defects: a mass assignment dropping tenant_id, a non-idempotent backfill, a bulk UPDATE relying on a request-scoped global scope, and engine-specific SQL.
effort_routing_evals.question: Defects found, false positives raised, and cost per genuine defect. Weight a missed tenancy leak far above a missed style nit.

effort_routing_evals.name: reconnaissance
effort_routing_evals.prompt: Find every place ProductStatus is used or duplicated, including non-obvious ones.
effort_routing_evals.question: Does higher effort or a stronger model find more of the 14 known sites — particularly the three non-obvious ones? If haiku/low finds them all, that settles the default for recon.

effort_routing_evals.name: context-versus-effort
configurations: sonnet/medium + a focused packet naming the two relevant methods
effort_routing_evals.question: Can context quality beat brute-force effort? This is one of the most decision-relevant comparisons in the suite.

effort_routing_evals.name: skill-versus-effort
effort_routing_evals.prompt: Add a Filament resource for Products following the project's admin-panel conventions.
effort_routing_evals.question: When does knowledge beat reasoning? Expected: the skill wins on convention adherence at lower cost.

effort_routing_evals.name: effort-escalation-validated
effort_routing_evals.prompt: Fix the caching inconsistency where two services disagree about invalidation order.
effort_routing_evals.fixture_setup: Requires a fixture with a genuinely subtle ordering bug — the current 33-file fixture is not sufficient and must be extended.
effort_routing_evals.question: Construct a task where medium misses and high succeeds. If no such task can be constructed, effort escalation is not earning its place and should be simplified out.

effort_routing_evals.name: model-escalation-validated
effort_routing_evals.prompt: Audit the multi-tenant authorization architecture for cross-tenant leakage and rank findings by exploitability.
effort_routing_evals.question: Is there a clear outcome improvement from the model step? Iteration 2 produced supporting evidence: an Opus step caught that the tenancy scope check is a truthiness test, extending the fail-open bug to authenticated-but-falsy tenant ids — a variant the Sonnet pass missed. Confirm or refute under controlled configurations.

effort_routing_evals.name: xhigh-justification
effort_routing_evals.prompt: We are overselling inventory under concurrent checkout across multiple app servers. Determine the correct locking and reservation architecture and prove it cannot violate the stock invariant.
effort_routing_evals.question: Does the maximum effort level produce a materially better answer? If not, say so and drop xhigh from the recommended policy rather than inventing a justification for it.

design_defects_found: SA/SD/SE/SG specified 'sonnet/medium + Skill(name)' configurations that are UNBUILDABLE: Skill(name) in agent frontmatter verified NOT to restrict invocation or trim the catalogue. Re-express as instruction-level narrowing or Read-by-path.
SA/SF/EG/EB assume the Laravel fixture / laravel-filament skill — stack bias; adapted to a generic conventions-skill test (same question, framework-neutral).

EH ('construct a task where medium misses and high succeeds') is selection-biased by design: constructing until the desired winner appears is benchmark gaming. Replaced with a fixed-task medium-vs-high comparison.
SB's 'total tool calls 16 or fewer' is an arbitrary numeric cap; compare against a measured baseline instead.
EI embeds an unverified prior claim as expected evidence, anchoring graders.
No control eval where all configurations should tie.
